\caption{Every control against every persistence feature: median over the embedding models of the real feature's AUROC minus the control's, at fixed query length without the query's own document (positive: the real arrangement separates the two chunkings more than the control). For $\Wone$ and the longest bar the random-bearing control is far too easy ($+0.3$ to $+0.5$, except the longest bar on Wikipedia, $+0.08$); for $\LTmax$ it is not. The corpus-bearing and shell-bearing controls leave small differences (at most about 0.05), except for the longest bar on the essays (about $+0.1$). Shading: vermillion where the real arrangement separates the chunkings better than the control, blue where worse; the tint grows with the difference and is full at $\pm0.3$, so a near-white cell means the control explains the feature. A difference of $+0.10$ means that, of every 100 pairs of neighbourhoods (one from each chunking), the real feature orders 10 more correctly than the control. The corpus-bearing row averages ten size-matched subsamples; the other rows use one. $^\ast$Two models (text-embedding-3-small, ModernBERT); not neutral for $\Wone$ (\cref{app:real}).}
